question.:question/problem: Let $f(x,y,z)=x - z - 3 y,$ where $x=t + 2 s$, $y=s - t$, $z=s + 2 t$. Calculate $\frac{∂f}{∂s}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/be/be6afcdd0ad9ae0d7ef377c4918442a64e1186c90c25e27ec6c224d816a602fd.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y,z)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t),y=y(s,t)$ and $z=z(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x,y$ and $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-3,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂s} & =2, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂s} & =1, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂s} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂s} & =(1)\cdot (2)+(-3)\cdot (1)+(-1)\cdot (1) \\  & =2 - 3 - 1 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/b5/b593a1b60fe8c1aef2c5c229ff426db350e6296b9ecb767494283f0fa3342072.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y,z)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t),y=y(s,t)$ and $z=z(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂t}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂t}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂t}+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂t}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x,y$ and $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=- \frac{5 y + 5 z}{x^{2}},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{5}{x},\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=\frac{5}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s$ and $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =- \frac{5 s^{2} + 5 t^{2}}{(s + t)^{2}}, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{5}{s + t}, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{5}{s + t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂t} & =1, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂t} & =0, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂t} & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂t} & =(\frac{- 5 s^{2} - 5 t^{2}}{(s + t)^{2}})\cdot (1)+(\frac{5}{s + t})\cdot (0)+(\frac{5}{s + t})\cdot (2 t) \\  & =\frac{- (5 s^{2} + 5 t^{2}) + 10 t (s + t)}{(s + t)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{- 5 s^{2} + 5 t^{2} + 10 s t}{(s + t)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $c_{1}=-5, c_{2}=10, c_{3}=5,$ and therefore

$$
{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}=-5 + 10 + 5=10.
$$

$$

$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s$ and $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{1}{t{s}^{2}}, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =- 5 e^{\ln{(s^{2} + t^{2} )}}=- 5 s^{2} - 5 t^{2}, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =3.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂t} & =s \\ \frac{∂y}{∂t} & =3 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂t} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂t} & =(10 s + 30 t + 2 s t)\cdot (s)+(10 s t)\cdot (3)+(- 24 s + 12 t)\cdot (-1) \\  & =10 s^{2} + 2 t s^{2} + 30 s t + 30 s t - 12 t + 24 s \\  & =- 12 t + 10 s^{2} + 24 s + 2 t s^{2} + 60 s t \\  & =2 (- 6 t + 5 s^{2} + 12 s + t s^{2} + 30 s t)\end{aligned}

Finally, $c_{1}=30, c_{2}=12, c_{3}=-6,$ and therefore

$$
{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}=30 + 12 - 6=36.

$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂t} & =1, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂t} & =0, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂t} & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂t} & =(\frac{- s^{2} - 5 t^{2}}{(s + t)^{2}})\cdot (1)+(\frac{1}{s + t})\cdot (0)+(\frac{5}{s + t})\cdot (2 t) \\  & =\frac{- (s^{2} + 5 t^{2}) + 10 t (s + t)}{(s + t)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{- s^{2} + 5 t^{2} + 10 s t}{(s + t)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

find the value of ${c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}.$

$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x,y$ and $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2yz,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}={y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s$ and $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =2 (- 4 s + 3 t) 3 s t=- 24 t s^{2} + 18 s t^{2}, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =(- 4 s + 3 t)^{2}=9 t^{2} + 16 s^{2} - 24 s t.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂t} & =3, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂t} & =3, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂t} & =3 s.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂t} & =(- \sin{(3 t )})\cdot (3)+(- 24 t s^{2} + 18 s t^{2})\cdot (3)+(9 t^{2} + 16 s^{2} - 24 s t)\cdot (3 s) \\  & =- 3 \sin{(3 t )} - 72 t s^{2} + 54 s t^{2} + 48 s^{3} - 72 t s^{2} + 27 s t^{2} \\  & =- 3 \sin{(3 t )} + 48 s^{3} - 144 t s^{2} + 81 s t^{2}.\end{aligned}

$$
{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+{c}_{3}=81 - 144 + 48=-15.
